pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql has a CHECK and a default of normal. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks that the seeded rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected.
The 'AC-2' test checks the '— high' and '— low' labels and that normal items get none.
The 'AC-3' test covers high, low and normal, including order.
The 'AC-4' test checks that / lists all items in id order.
The 'AC-5' test asserts the exact nav HTML for all four views.
The 'AC-6' test checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty and __proto__.
The 'AC-7' test covers the per-priority message and 'No items yet.' in every view of an empty table.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'. The 'AC-8' test checks it, and the traffic-config check now accepts query strings.

findings.what: The last commit ('Follow-up edits') deleted the state test 'All priorities: every item, All current'. The spec's States table has an 'All priorities' row: every item, no message, All current. No single test now sets up that state. AC-4 checks the list, and AC-5 checks that All is current. Nothing asserts that no message shows. The deletion has no spec justification, and the PR says no tests were deleted or loosened.
findings.fix: Restore the state test, and also assert that message(html) is null.

findings.what: The commit left a stray blank line after `describe("states", () => {`.

lenses.note: The change follows the spec and its decisions: existing items are normal, and only high and low are labelled. Nothing was added beyond the ask.
All 8 acceptance items have a test that names them. The State table row 'All priorities' lost its test in the last commit (see the finding).
The tests look able to fail if the code were wrong. I did not run them here. CI runs them on every push. The deleted state test is a finding.
The README describes the filter. The PR body notes the traffic route check change.
The 400 for an invalid or empty value, the parameterised query and the COUNT used to choose the empty message all look correct.
The priority value is checked against an allow-list and bound as a parameter. Titles are escaped. The route regex still refuses spaces and #.
Only a minimal server-rendered nav was added, with no styling or UI files. I treated it as covered by the qa and spec checks.
No browser flow was demonstrated. The PR says there are no screenshots, and the tests cover the rendered HTML.
The claim 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' is not accurate, because the last commit deleted a state test. The other claims match the diff.
